runs.name: getup_easy_lean
runs.config: mild lean only (20-40deg), home joints, no restore

runs.name: getup_s1_lean_ft
runs.config: mild lean only, restore walk policy

runs.name: getup_s2_mixed_ft
runs.config: 35% fallen + mild lean, restore walk policy

reward_reference.note: A policy that simply stayed at the lean start would score about +2300 per episode; every run scored about -2900 to -3200, i.e. the robot falls even from a mild lean.

exploration_ceiling.test: random uniform actions, 500 steps, 12 seeds, from the getup start distribution
exploration_ceiling.conclusion: From a fully fallen start, random exploration cannot reach an upright attitude, so the standing reward is unreachable by chance.

model_integrity.test: official BEST_WALK_ONNX_2 starting from the home keyframe, 10 s, both scenes
model_integrity.conclusion: Adding the trunk/head collision boxes did not change the physics: the verified walk policy behaves identically. The getup failures are a learning problem, not a model problem.

fixed_blocker.issue: Upstream open_duck_mini_v2.xml gives collision geometry only to the two foot soles (3 of 47 geoms), so a fallen robot has nothing to rest on and sinks through the floor (measured base height -0.169 m, up_z about -1).
fixed_blocker.fix: make_getup_model.py derives open_duck_mini_v2_getup.xml / scene_flat_terrain_getup.xml with trunk and head collision boxes; the originals are untouched.
fixed_blocker.verified: Robot settles at base z=0.097 when dropped at 90 degrees instead of sinking.

recommendations: Train far longer: the verified walk policy used 150M timesteps; these runs used 6-12M (about 300-600 PPO updates).
Add a reference-motion or scripted-getup imitation signal; pure sparse standing reward is not reachable from a full fall.
Stage the curriculum much more gradually and verify the start poses rest on the floor without an initial impact impulse.
